region: Baghdad, Babylon, the southern marshes and the Kurdistan Region
title: Iraq — Between the Rivers, Written in Clay and Reed
subtitle: Mesopotamia's cities, the Ahwar marshes and living pilgrim cities: a concept that cannot currently be recommended
summary: Ziggurat of Ur, Babylon, the Chibayish marshes, Baghdad's book street and the Kurdish north make an exceptional concept, but official advice currently advises against all or all-but-essential travel across the route.
introduction: Iraq holds the first cities, the earliest writing and one of the world's great wetlands. The imagined route would run from Baghdad's booksellers on Al-Mutanabbi Street to the rebuilt walls of Babylon, the Ziggurat of Ur near Nasiriyah and the reed houses of Chibayish in the Ahwar marshes, then north to Erbil's citadel and the Rawanduz gorge. Najaf, Karbala and Kadhimiya add living Shia pilgrimage, and Samarra's spiral minaret an Abbasid capital. It is presented here as a cultural and geographic concept only: current official advice does not allow us to recommend it, and no operational itinerary is offered.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman's trip is self-driven and tent-based over empty desert; Iraq would be about deep time and people, with hired drivers, guesthouses and mudhif stays, and nearly all independence removed by checkpoints and advisories.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Few packages go beyond Baghdad's museums; the concept would link Sumerian ruins, a marsh homestay culture and Kurdish mountains, but any real offer would be a security-managed group tour, not independent travel.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other portfolio destination combines cuneiform-era cities, a Mesopotamian marsh civilisation and pilgrimage cities in one journey; this is also why its absence from the eligible list should be reviewed if advice ever changes.

duration.note: Indicative length only; no day-by-day plan is offered for an excluded route.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: After Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr (about 9-10 March), before summer heat; marshes are green and mild, and Nowruz (20-21 March) is celebrated in the Kurdistan Region. Only relevant if advice changes.

februarySuitability.summary: Cool and pleasant in the south, cold and wet in the Kurdish mountains; Ramadan from about 8 February limits daytime food and some opening hours.

marchSuitability.summary: Mild in the south (about 25 C days) and green in the north; Ramadan ends about 9 March, so the second half is easier.

february.notes: Erbil is colder, with snow possible on the mountains near Amedi and Rawanduz.

march.notes: Dust storms can begin in spring.

geography.summary: The Tigris and Euphrates alluvial plain, the reed marshes of the south and the Zagros foothills of Kurdistan.
geography.distinctive: The Ahwar, one of the largest inland delta wetlands in the Middle East, where Ma'dan communities live on reed islands, set against nearby Sumerian ruins in desert.

signatureExperiences.title: Dawn at the Ziggurat of Ur
signatureExperiences.description: Walk the restored 4,000-year-old ziggurat and the nearby royal tombs site near Nasiriyah.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of the best-preserved Sumerian monuments, within the Ahwar UNESCO property.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Would require a licensed guide and local security arrangements; not currently recommendable.

signatureExperiences.title: A night in the Chibayish marshes
signatureExperiences.description: Boat through reed channels and sleep in a mudhif guesthouse.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A living wetland culture with few parallels worldwide.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Local boatmen and guesthouses; advisories name Dhi Qar as orange or all-but-essential.

signatureExperiences.title: Babylon to Karbala by road
signatureExperiences.description: Visit Babylon's reconstructed walls, then Najaf and Karbala.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Pairs Neo-Babylonian ruins with living pilgrim cities.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Hired driver and guide; Najaf and Karbala are all-but-essential per FCDO and orange per NL.
